## Motivation Port the diffusion W8A8 support from #29048 into a separate PR. This adds online INT8 quantization for unquantized FP16/BF16 diffusion transformers on Ascend NPU. The SRT LLM and MoE changes from #29048 are outside this PR. ## Modifications - Add `NPUOnlineW8A8DiffusionConfig` and its linear method: quantize weights after loading, dynamically quantize activations per token, and return outputs in the original FP16/BF16 dtype. - Register `w8a8_int` for diffusion and forward `--quantization-ignored-layers` so selected layers stay in checkpoint precision. - Reuse the shared Ascend dynamic INT8 linear backend, with optional RMSNorm and SwiGLU activation-quantization fusion and floating-point fallbacks. - Update `--quantization` help and diffusion quantization documentation. ## Accuracy Tests BF16: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a563b48a-ccff-4ad0-af90-a46d27033a3f W8A8 with `--component-quantization-ignored-layers.transformer token_refiner final_layer condition_proj adaln_proj`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9006b85-b7d0-4bc9-b59f-bae212b4c5cc FULL W8A8: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1685e35-46df-4fab-80be-dbb98bafbadb ### MiniMax-H3
Launch command on 8 Ascend NPUs (TP=2, SP=4): ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ sglang serve \ --model-path /home/weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 8 \ --port 30010 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 4 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --component-quantizations.transformer w8a8_int \ --component-quantization-ignored-layers.transformer \ token_refiner final_layer condition_proj adaln_proj \ --component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload transformer=resident ``` Submit a text-to-video-and-audio request, wait for completion, and download the MP4 ([cookbook example](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/474a63e8c7351a21f5337ab60e2c5c611ce56516/docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx#4-generate-video-and-audio); requires `jq`): ```bash video_id=$( curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3", "prompt": "At night, while their owner sleeps in a bedroom, three cats march in loudly playing tiny brass instruments, then abruptly file out.", "seconds": 5, "task": "t2va", "conditions": [], "target": { "short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0 }, "num_outputs_per_prompt": 1, "num_inference_steps": 50, "flow_shift": 12.0, "audio_flow_shift": 3.0, "seed": 1101 }' | jq -r '.id' ) while true; do status=$(curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos/${video_id}" | jq -r '.status') [ "$status" = "completed" ] && break [ "$status" = "failed" ] && exit 1 sleep 1 done curl -sS -L "http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/videos/${video_id}/content" \ -o minimax-h3-t2va.mp4 ```
BF16: W8A8 with `--component-quantization-ignored-layers.transformer token_refiner final_layer condition_proj adaln_proj`: FULL W8A8: Local validation passed: Ruff lint and formatting, isort, Python syntax parsing, and `git diff --check`. The attached MiniMax-H3 outputs were generated on Ascend NPUs. +For online INT8 quantization on Ascend, load the original FP16/BF16 checkpoint
+and add `--quantization w8a8_int`. On A14B models this selects both
+transformers; `--transformer-quantization w8a8_int` selects only the primary

 - `--tp-size {TP_SIZE}`: Tensor parallelism size (only for the encoder; should not be larger than 1 if text encoder offload is enabled, as layer-wise offload plus prefetch is faster)

@@ -1245,6 +1245,87 @@ MindStudio-ModelSlim (msModelSlim) is a model offline quantization compression t
     - [x]  ```mxfp8``` linear with online quantization (`--quantization mxfp8`)
     - [x]  ```W4A4_MXFP4``` / ```W4A4_MXFP4_DUALSCALE``` linear with offline quantization (msmodelslim pre-quantized weights)
     - [x]  ```mxfp4_npu``` linear with online quantization (`--quantization mxfp4_npu`)
+    - [x]  ```w8a8_int``` linear with online quantization on Ascend (`--quantization w8a8_int`)
+
+## Online W8A8 INT8 on Ascend
+
+Use `--quantization w8a8_int` with an original FP16/BF16 diffusion checkpoint
+on Ascend NPU. Follow the
+[NPU installation guide](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation)
+and install compatible CANN, PyTorch, and torch_npu versions before running.
+The backend requires `npu_dynamic_quant` and `npu_quant_matmul`.
+
+Weights are quantized per output channel as each complete local weight is loaded,
+after fused projections are assembled and tensor-parallel slicing is applied.
+The loader releases that weight's FP16/BF16 buffer immediately, reducing peak NPU
+loading memory. FSDP/DTensor loading keeps the existing post-load conversion path.
+Activations are dynamically quantized per token. Linear outputs retain the input FP16/BF16
+dtype. This online method does not require calibration or a ModelSlim
+`quant_model_description.json`; use the existing ModelSlim loading path for
+pre-quantized checkpoints.
+
+For Wan 2.2 T2V-A14B, the following example uses eight Ascend NPUs with TP2
+and SP4:
+
+```bash
+sglang generate \
+  --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
+  --num-gpus 8 \
+  --tp-size 2 \
+  --sp-degree 4 \
+  --attention-backend laser_attn \
+  --quantization w8a8_int \
+  --quantization-ignored-layers blocks.0 \
+  --prompt "a fox walking through neon rain" \
+  --save-output
+```
+
+The following models integrate this online linear path. Target-NPU
+correctness and generation quality remain pending validation for each model.
+The component column describes global `--quantization w8a8_int` selection.
+
+| Model | Transformer components | Activation | Target-NPU validation |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| MiniMax-H3 | `transformer` | SwiGLU | Pending |
+| Wan 2.2 T2V-A14B | `transformer`, `transformer_2` | GELU | Pending |
+| Wan 2.2 I2V-A14B | `transformer`, `transformer_2` | GELU | Pending |
+| Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B | `transformer` | GELU | Pending |
+
+Use the [Wan 2.2 cookbook](/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan2.2) or
+[MiniMax-H3 cookbook](/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3) for model and
+input settings. MiniMax-H3 optionally fuses SwiGLU or residual RMSNorm with
+activation quantization when the installed NPU operators support them; otherwise it
+uses separate activation, normalization, and quantization operations.
+
+On Wan 2.2 A14B, global `--quantization w8a8_int` applies to both
+`transformer` and `transformer_2`. To select only the primary transformer,
+replace the global flag with `--transformer-quantization w8a8_int`.
+The example above keeps block 0 in checkpoint precision on both A14B
+transformers. To select both components explicitly while excluding block 0
+only from the primary transformer:
+
+```bash
+sglang generate \
+  --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
+  --num-gpus 8 \
+  --tp-size 2 \
+  --sp-degree 4 \
+  --attention-backend laser_attn \
+  --component-quantizations.transformer w8a8_int \
+  --component-quantizations.transformer_2 w8a8_int \
+  --component-quantization-ignored-layers.transformer blocks.0 \
+  --prompt "a fox walking through neon rain" \
+  --save-output
+```
+
+Use `--quantization-ignored-layers blocks.0` to keep block 0 of each selected
+transformer in checkpoint precision; with the global quantization flag,
+this component-local prefix is applied to both A14B transformers. To exclude
+layers from just one explicitly selected component, use
+`--component-quantization-ignored-layers.transformer blocks.0` together with
+`--transformer-quantization w8a8_int`.
+
+Existing BF16 cookbook benchmarks do not measure this online W8A8 configuration.

+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

+def _supports_add_rmsnorm_int8(device: torch.device, dtype: torch.dtype, width: int):
+    try:
+        x = torch.zeros((1, width), device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        weight = torch.ones(width, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        data, _, residual, scale, _ = torch.ops.npu.npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_quant(
+            x, x, weight, epsilon=1e-6
+        )
+        return (
+            data.dtype == torch.int8
+            and data.shape == x.shape
+            and residual.dtype == dtype
+            and residual.shape == x.shape
+            and scale.dtype == torch.float32
+            and scale.shape == (1,)
+        )
+    except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
+        raise
+    except (AttributeError, NotImplementedError, RuntimeError):
+        return False
+
+
+class BaseNormalization(ABC):
+    @abstractmethod
+    def _apply_norm(self, *args, **kwargs): ...
+
+
+class NPURMSNorm(BaseNormalization):
+    def _apply_norm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weight: torch.Tensor,
+        eps: float | None,
+        residual: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        *,
+        preserve_residual_rounding: bool = False,
+    ):
+        if eps is None:
+            eps = torch.finfo(x.dtype).eps
+        if residual is not None:
+            if preserve_residual_rounding:
+                # Preserve the model's low-precision residual addition.
+                x = residual = residual + x
+            else:
+                out, _, residual_out = torch.ops.npu.npu_add_rms_norm(
+                    residual, x, weight, eps
+                )
+                return out, residual_out
+
+        if preserve_residual_rounding and (
+            x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+            or weight.dtype != x.dtype
+            or weight.device != x.device
+            or x.numel() == 0
+            or not hasattr(torch.ops.npu, "npu_rms_norm")
+        ):
+            out = F.rms_norm(x, (weight.shape[-1],), weight, eps)
+        else:
+            out = torch.ops.npu.npu_rms_norm(x, weight, eps)[0]
+        return out if residual is None else (out, residual)
+
+
+class NPURMSNormQuant(NPURMSNorm):
+    @staticmethod
+    def is_supported(
+        x: torch.Tensor, residual: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor | None
+    ) -> bool:
+        if (
+            x.device.type != "npu"
+            or x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+            or x.ndim != 2
+            or x.numel() == 0
+            or residual.shape != x.shape
+            or residual.dtype != x.dtype
+            or residual.device != x.device
+            or weight is None
+            or weight.shape != (x.shape[-1],)
+            or weight.dtype != x.dtype
+            or weight.device != x.device
+        ):
+            return False
+        return _supports_add_rmsnorm_int8(x.device, x.dtype, x.shape[-1])
+
+    def _apply_norm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weight: torch.Tensor,
+        eps: float | None,
+        residual: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        *,
+        preserve_residual_rounding: bool = False,
+    ):
+        if residual is None or not self.is_supported(x, residual, weight):
+            return super()._apply_norm(
+                x,
+                weight,
+                eps,
+                residual,
+                preserve_residual_rounding=preserve_residual_rounding,
+            )
+        if eps is None:
+            eps = torch.finfo(x.dtype).eps
+        from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.npu.quantization.linear_method_npu import (
+            _INT8Activation,

+
+        data, _, residual_out, scales, _ = torch.ops.npu.npu_add_rms_norm_dynamic_quant(
+            x, residual, weight, epsilon=eps
+        )
+        return _INT8Activation(data, scales, x.dtype), residual_out
+
+

+    return NPURMSNormQuant() if quantize else NPURMSNorm()
